scenes.text: Have you ever wondered why Popeye got super strength from eating spinach, when it actually started with a single, tiny typo?
In 1870, a scientist calculating the nutrients in spinach misplaced a decimal point, accidentally multiplying its iron content by ten.
This simple mistake created a massive global superfood myth that lasted for decades before anyone noticed the error.
Did you fall for this giant green lie growing up, or do you actually like spinach?

meta.title: The Single Typo That Fooled The Entire World #shorts
meta.description:
Have you ever wondered why Popeye got super strength from eating spinach? It all started with a single, tiny typo. In 1870, a German scientist was calculating the nutritional value of green vegetables. When writing his findings, he accidentally misplaced a decimal point. Instead of writing 3.5 milligrams of iron, he wrote 35 milligrams! This simple mistake made spinach look ten times healthier than it actually was. The public went wild, believing spinach was a miracle superfood, which eventually inspired the famous cartoon sailor. By the time scientists corrected the mistake decades later, the myth was already locked into history. Now you know why your parents forced you to eat it. Did you fall for this giant green lie, or do you actually like spinach? Subscribe for more wild stories!
